name: PLA+ (Toughened PLA)
chemical_makeup: PLA-majority blend (PLLA/PDLA polylactide) compounded with an undisclosed impact modifier / elastomeric toughening additive; manufacturers describe it only as 'modified based on PLA material' and publish no filler or co-monomer content
summary: Base PLA plus a proprietary impact modifier — same lactide chemistry, mechanical delta only. Versus base PLA it trades some stiffness and tensile strength for markedly better impact toughness and layer adhesion (Bambu measures higher elongation in Z than in XY, the toughening signature), runs hotter at the top of the range (210-250 °C vs 190-230 °C), wants a hotter/longer dry (55 °C/8 h vs 45-55 °C/6 h) and prints slower than base PLA (eSUN and colorFabb recommend 40-50 mm/s). Heat resistance is unchanged: HDT still ~53-58 °C.

printing.notes: Delta vs base PLA: the usable nozzle band extends higher and is brand-split — eSUN PLA+ 210-230 °C and colorFabb Tough PLA 210-230 °C sit on top of base PLA, while Bambu PLA Tough+ specifies 220-250 °C with spec samples printed at 245 °C, notably hotter than base PLA and probably a different toughening compound. Bed 35-65 °C (eSUN rec 45 °C, colorFabb 50-60 °C, Bambu rec 55 °C). Full part cooling as with base PLA. The other real delta is speed: eSUN recommends 40 mm/s (tested to 100 mm/s) and colorFabb 40-50 mm/s, well below base PLA's 100+ mm/s, so this is not the grade to pick for throughput — see pla-hf. Bambu lists an optional 25-45 °C chamber for dimensional consistency; it is not a requirement, and as with all PLA grades an enclosed machine should be run with the door/lid open to avoid heat creep.

feeding.notes: Rigid, unfilled and non-abrasive, so it feeds identically to base PLA: any extruder, standard brass-compatible drive gears and PTFE, no spool-side assistant. Bambu ships PLA Tough+ as an explicitly AMS-supported product, matching base PLA's plain 'yes' rather than the 'conditional' rating carried by silk and filled PLA grades. No shore hardness applies — this is a rigid grade, not a flexible.

drying.dryness_validation: No popping/crackling or visible steam at the nozzle; glossy, consistent extrudate; minimal stringing on a retraction test — same checks as base PLA
drying.notes: Delta vs base PLA (45-55 °C / 4-8 h): Bambu specifies 55 °C for 8 h in a blast/dry-box oven or 65-75 °C for 12 h using the printer heatbed, hotter and longer than typical base-PLA practice. eSUN and colorFabb publish no drying parameters, so for those brands standard PLA drying is the working assumption (unverified). Separately, Bambu recommends post-print annealing at 50-60 °C for 6-12 h to raise heat resistance — a post-process, not a drying step, and the opposite of lw-pla, where annealing is actively harmful.

storage.recommendations: Sealed bag or drybox with desiccant between uses; tolerates open-air storage in a dry room like base PLA

price.notes: eSUN PLA+ about $22.99/kg (1 kg spool, eSUN store, confirmed); Bambu PLA Tough+ about $29.99/kg and colorFabb Tough PLA about $40-45/kg (both unverified — store figures not confirmed by fetch). Roughly a $5-15/kg premium over base PLA's $14-35/kg band.

recommended: cosplay props needing more durability than base PLA
not_recommended: continuously loaded structural parts (creep, as with base PLA)

properties.notes: Density is brand-split but all within base-PLA range: eSUN 1.23, colorFabb 1.24, Bambu PLA Tough+ 1.21 g/cm³ — 1.23 recorded. Tensile figures do NOT agree across brands because the test methods differ: eSUN 63 MPa (injection-moulded spline, which overstates FDM-printed parts), colorFabb 55 MPa (printed X-Y), Bambu 34.9±1 MPa X-Y / 20.9±1 MPa Z. Elongation at break: eSUN 20 %, colorFabb 8.6 %, Bambu 5.1 % X-Y / 10.4 % Z — Bambu's Z elongation exceeding X-Y is the clearest evidence of the toughening package working on interlayer bonds. Impact: eSUN IZOD 9 kJ/m², colorFabb Charpy notched 5.8 kJ/m², Bambu 80.6±9.5 kJ/m² X-Y; different tests, not comparable. Thermal (Bambu): Tg 61 °C, HDT 58 °C at 1.8 MPa, melt 151 °C; eSUN HDT 53 °C; colorFabb lists Tg/HDT as N/A. HDT here is at 1.8 MPa, not the schema-default 0.45 MPa. Shrinkage not published by any brand (unverified) — assume base PLA's 0.3-0.5 %.

compatibility.notes: Same PLA-family bonding behaviour as the base entry: welds to itself and other PLA grades, does not weld to PETG/ABS/ASA/PC/PA/PP. Commonly paired with lw-pla (tough ribs inside foamed skins) and with base PLA for multi-colour work. Standard PLA breakaway or water-soluble PVA/BVOH supports, as recommended by colorFabb and Polymaker for their tough PLA lines.

plate_recommendations.notes: Same as base PLA — adheres at 45-60 °C with no release agent, and the textured grain suits the grade's naturally matte finish. No special surface needed.
Backfilled from plate entry (Phase E reciprocity): Behaves as base PLA; no aid needed.
Backfilled from plate entry (Phase E reciprocity): As base PLA.
Backfilled from plate entry (Phase E reciprocity): As base PLA.
Backfilled from plate entry (Phase E reciprocity): As base PLA; toughened blends make no measurable difference to release behaviour.
Backfilled from plate entry (Phase E reciprocity): Toughened PLA blends sometimes want the upper end of the range; stay under the plate's low thermal ceiling.
Backfilled from plate entry (Phase E reciprocity): As base PLA.

emissions.notes: No measured difference from base PLA — no styrene, caprolactam or foaming agent involved, and the emission class stays far below ABS/ASA. The one caveat is that Bambu's grade runs up to 250 °C, ~20 °C hotter than base PLA, which nudges particulate output up; and because the impact-modifier chemistry is undisclosed, any trace difference in emitted species is unverified. Ventilate for continuous printing in an occupied room.

safety_notes: No formal FDA/NSF food-contact certification was found for any brand's PLA+, and the toughening additive is undisclosed — treat as not food-safe, a stricter call than base PLA's 'conditional'.
additional_notes: PLA+ is a compounded grade, not a different base resin — 'PLA+', 'PLA Pro' and 'Tough PLA' are marketing names covering different proprietary formulations, which is why brand-to-brand mechanical figures diverge so widely. Bambu notes resistance to most oils and greases.

provenance.conflicts: Tensile strength disagrees by a factor of ~1.8 across brands (eSUN 63 MPa injection-moulded, colorFabb 55 MPa printed X-Y, Bambu 34.9 MPa X-Y) because the test specimens differ — recorded as a 35-63 MPa range rather than reconciled. Impact strength is reported in incompatible tests (IZOD 9 kJ/m², Charpy notched 5.8 kJ/m², Bambu 80.6 kJ/m²) and cannot be compared. Nozzle temperature is brand-split: 210-230 °C for eSUN/colorFabb vs 220-250 °C for Bambu. HDT: Bambu 58 °C at 1.8 MPa vs eSUN 53 °C (load unstated) vs colorFabb N/A. Drying parameters exist only for Bambu; eSUN/colorFabb values are assumed from base PLA (unverified). Prices for Bambu and colorFabb are estimates, not confirmed store figures.
